sourcedFrom: VOLQUARTSEN SUMMIT RIFLE OWNER’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision code printed (UNKNOWN — not printed in the document)
cleanIntro: The Summit is a straight-pull rimfire rifle and it comes apart with hex keys and punches, not by hand: one 1/8 inch takedown action screw frees the barrelled action from the chassis, two 3/16 inch cross pins release the trigger guard, and a 5/16 inch cross pin at the top rear of the receiver frees the bolt. ⛔ The single most expensive mistake you can make on this rifle is a cleaning rod from the muzzle: Volquartsen says it voids the warranty and hurts accuracy. Breech to muzzle, pull-through only.

steps.title: Safe, magazine out, bolt back, and EYES in the chamber
steps.action: Put the safety in the safe position, remove the magazine, pull the bolt to the rear and eject any chambered cartridge. Your last act is a visual inspection of the chamber — Volquartsen makes that the final step, not the first assumption.
steps.prose: Four actions in one order, and the look is what ends it.
steps.quote:
in the safe position, remove the magazine, pull the bolt to 
the rear, and eject the chambered cartridge. 
Your final step is to visually inspect the chamber.
steps.cite: VOLQUARTSEN SUMMIT RIFLE OWNER’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision code printed — Unloading, p.8

steps.title: Glasses on — and the rifle must be unloaded to strip it
steps.action: Safety glasses before anything moves. Volquartsen states it plainly for the strip: the firearm must be unloaded during disassembly, and glasses should be worn at all times when working with any firearm.
steps.prose: There are two punches and a spring-loaded trigger group ahead of you.
steps.quote:
The firearm must be unloaded 
during the disassembly. Safety 
glasses should be worn at all times 
when working with any firearm.
steps.cite: VOLQUARTSEN SUMMIT RIFLE OWNER’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision code printed — Disassembly, p.8

steps.title: 1/8 inch hex on the takedown action screw, underneath
steps.action: The takedown action screw is at the BOTTOM of the rifle. A 1/8 inch hex key wrench backs it out; then the barrelled action lifts out of the chassis.
steps.prose: One screw is the whole join. Set it somewhere it cannot roll.
steps.quote:
Remove the takedown action 
	 screw—located at the bottom of
	 the rifle—using a 1⁄8˝ hex key
	 wrench.
steps.cite: VOLQUARTSEN SUMMIT RIFLE OWNER’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision code printed — Disassembly, step 2, p.9

steps.title: ⚠ The trigger guard comes out BEFORE the bolt — two 3/16 inch cross pins
steps.action: The bolt cannot come out until the trigger guard does. Use a 1/8 inch punch to drift the two 3/16 inch cross pins at the bottom of the receiver, and the trigger guard slides out.
steps.prose: This order surprises people who know rimfire rifles. On the Summit it is not optional.
steps.quote: Use a 1⁄8˝ punch to remove the two 3⁄16˝ cross pins located at the bottom of the receiver.
steps.cite: VOLQUARTSEN SUMMIT RIFLE OWNER’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision code printed — Disassembly, step 4, p.9

steps.title: ⛔ Do NOT take the trigger guard further apart
steps.action: Volquartsen recommends against disassembling the trigger guard any further. Clean its inside periodically with an aerosol gun cleaner that leaves NO residue. ⛔ Do NOT spray oil onto the hammer/sear engagement area, and take excess overspray off with a cotton swab.
steps.prose: Oil on a rimfire sear is how a trigger gets heavier and less predictable, and this is a rifle people buy for its trigger.
steps.quote:
DO NOT spray any oil onto the
	 hammer/sear engagement area.
steps.cite: VOLQUARTSEN SUMMIT RIFLE OWNER’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision code printed — Disassembly, step 5, p.9

steps.title: 1/4 inch punch on the 5/16 inch cross pin, then lift the bolt out
steps.action: Lay the barrelled action UPSIDE DOWN on a flat, padded surface and drift the 5/16 inch cross pin at the top rear of the receiver with a 1/4 inch punch. Then pull the bolt handle to the rear and lift the bolt upward and out. ⚠ Removing the bolt handle and operating rail is NOT recommended.
steps.prose: Padded and upside down is the instruction, and it is there so the pin does not mark the receiver on the way through.
steps.quote: Pull the bolt handle to the rear and remove the bolt by lifting upward.
steps.cite: VOLQUARTSEN SUMMIT RIFLE OWNER’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision code printed — Disassembly, step 7, p.10

steps.title: ⛔ Do NOT take the bolt apart — clean the receiver instead
steps.action: Volquartsen is explicit: DO NOT disassemble the bolt any further. What wants attention is the inside of the RECEIVER — cleaned and MINIMALLY lubricated on a regular basis with any quality gun oil.
steps.prose: "Minimally" is the operative word on a rimfire. Oil collects wax and grit and then holds it against the bolt.
steps.quote:
DO NOT disassemble the bolt any
	 further. The inside of the receiver
	 should be cleaned and minimally
	 lubricated on a regular basis
	 using any quality gun oil.
steps.cite: VOLQUARTSEN SUMMIT RIFLE OWNER’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision code printed — Disassembly, step 8, p.10

steps.title: ⛔ BREECH TO MUZZLE, PULL-THROUGH ONLY — a rod from the muzzle voids the warranty
steps.action: Clean the barrel ONLY from breech to muzzle, with a pull-through system. ⛔ Any use of a cleaning rod from the muzzle end voids the warranty and greatly affects accuracy. This is the one rule on this rifle that costs money to break.
steps.prose: The crown is the last thing the bullet touches. A rod entering there is why the warranty language exists.
steps.quote:
The barrel should be cleaned only from breech to muzzle 
using a pull-through cleaning system.
steps.cite: VOLQUARTSEN SUMMIT RIFLE OWNER’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision code printed — Barrel Cleaning, p.12
steps.warn: Any use of a cleaning rod from the muzzle end will void the warranty and greatly affect accuracy.

steps.title: Every 500-600 rounds — and the chamber more often, cotton swab only
steps.action: Volquartsen's interval for the barrel is approximately every 500 to 600 rounds. ⚠ The CHAMBER may need cleaning more often, and only with a cotton swab — not a brush, not a rod.
steps.prose: For a high-volume rimfire shooter that is a couple of range days, not a season.
steps.aside:
It may be necessary to clean the chamber area on a more 
frequent basis using only a cotton swab.
steps.quote:
We recommend that you clean the barrel approximately 
every 500-600 rounds.
steps.cite: VOLQUARTSEN SUMMIT RIFLE OWNER’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision code printed — Barrel Cleaning, p.12

steps.title: Bolt, trigger guard, action, screw — and check the ammunition
steps.action: Reverse the strip: bolt in and its 5/16 inch cross pin seated, trigger guard in with both 3/16 inch pins, barrelled action into the chassis, takedown action screw home with the 1/8 inch hex. ⚠ Then the ammunition: this rifle is built for 17 Mach 2 or 22 LR, and CCI Stinger is NOT recommended in it — the cartridge is oversized.
steps.prose: The Stinger warning is model-specific and it is a chamber-dimension problem, not a preference.
steps.quote: CCI® Stinger ammo is NOT recommended for use in this rifle due to the oversized cartridge.
steps.cite: VOLQUARTSEN SUMMIT RIFLE OWNER’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision code printed — Ammunition, p.13

deepAbsentReason: Volquartsen's Summit Rifle manual stops where its own disassembly stops, and it says so twice: "It is not recommended to disassemble the trigger guard any further" and "DO NOT disassemble the bolt any further." Beyond the bolt and the trigger guard the book publishes no procedure at all — no barrel removal, no extractor or firing-pin work, no trigger adjustment. This listing therefore has NO deep clean, and nothing deeper is invented for it.

cleaning.name: BARREL — THE RULE THAT VOIDS THE WARRANTY
tasks: ⛔ Breech to muzzle ONLY, pull-through system
⛔ Never a cleaning rod from the muzzle end
Chamber more often, with a cotton swab only

cleaning.name: RECEIVER AND BOLT
tasks: Inside of the receiver cleaned and MINIMALLY lubricated, any quality gun oil
Bolt handle and operating rail left installed

cleaning.name: TRIGGER GUARD
tasks: Inside cleaned periodically with a residue-free aerosol gun cleaner
⛔ No oil on the hammer/sear engagement area
Overspray removed with a cotton swab

reassembly: Bolt in, 5/16 inch cross pin seated at the top rear of the receiver.
Trigger guard in, both 3/16 inch cross pins driven home.
Barrelled action back into the chassis.
Takedown action screw tightened with the 1/8 inch hex key.
Ammunition confirmed: 17 Mach 2 or 22 LR — ⛔ not CCI Stinger.
fncheck: Magazine out and the chamber checked by eye. Work the bolt through full travel and confirm it runs free and the bolt handle and operating rail are seated. Confirm the takedown action screw is tight and both cross pins are flush. Dry-fire only with the safety understood and the muzzle safe. ⚠ Confirm the ammunition before loading — CCI Stinger can cause a bore obstruction in this rifle and voids the warranty.
